questions.q: According to this lesson, how does a data governance program actually get funded?
options: The same way any other initiative does — a defined problem, a proposed solution, a resource ask, and a way to measure results
By asserting that governance is important enough to fund on its own
By waiting for a compliance audit to force the decision
By purchasing a data catalog tool first and requesting budget afterward
questions.explain: Governance competes for budget like any initiative — it needs a defined problem, a proposed solution, a resource ask, and measurable anticipated value, not an assertion of importance.

questions.q: What are the four components of a credible business case described in this lesson?
options: The problem in business terms, the proposed solution and scope, required resources, and anticipated value with a way to measure it
A maturity model, an operating model, a RACI chart, and a policy library
A vendor comparison, a budget forecast, a staffing plan, and a risk register
A mission statement, a vision statement, a charter, and a council roster
questions.explain: The four components are: the problem framed in business terms, the proposed solution and its scope, the resources required, and the anticipated value along with how it will be measured.

questions.q: Why would a CFO and a business unit leader be given different framings of the same governance proposal?
options: Because each stakeholder is actually weighing a different risk — cost avoidance for a CFO versus speed and trust for a business leader
Because business unit leaders do not have authority to approve budget
Because CFOs only approve proposals that mention compliance
Because the scope of the program changes depending on the audience
questions.explain: The underlying program is the same, but a CFO weighs cost avoidance and audit exposure while a business unit leader weighs speed and trust in the data their team relies on — so the framing adapts to what each audience is actually evaluating.

questions.q: What role does the Lesson 25 readiness-assessment gap list play in the business case?
options: It supplies the specific evidence — the actual weak dimension and visible pain — that keeps the case from reading as a generic pitch
It is a separate document unrelated to the business case
It replaces the need for a resource ask
It is only used after the pilot has already launched
questions.explain: A business case written without the gap list tends to repeat generic language about 'trust' and 'quality' — the gap list is what makes the case specific to the organization's actual situation.

questions.q: What is a common way business cases fail to deliver on their promises later, according to this lesson?
options: Underselling the people cost — the time commitment required from staff — when listing required resources
Including too many trackable metrics in the value section
Scoping the initial ask too narrowly as a pilot
Naming an executive sponsor in the resources section
questions.explain: Underselling the real time and staffing cost is flagged as the single most common way a business case sets up a program to under-deliver once work actually begins.
